title: Relative ampleness of spaces descends fpqc locally
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $L$ be a line module on $X$. A line module on an algebraic space is an $\mathcal O$-module on its small etale site locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a morphism $a:Z\to W$, write $a^*M=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{a^{-1}\mathcal O_W}a^{-1}M$ using its canonical ringed etale topoi [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]; on schemes use the corresponding ordinary invertible module [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence, def-sc-invertible-module]. For a line module $N$ on a space $Z$ over a scheme $B$, relatively ample means that $Z$ is a scheme and $N$ is ample on the inverse image of every affine open of $B$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Let $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering by schemes [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Put $X_i=X\times_TT_i$ and let $L_i$ be the tensor pullback of $L$ to $X_i$. Then $L$ is relatively ample over $T$ if and only if every $L_i$ is relatively ample over $T_i$. This equivalence includes that $X$ is a scheme when all the $X_i$ are schemes with the indicated relative ampleness; it requires no properness or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), specialized to scheme bases and scheme covering members; spaces-divisors.tex Tags 0D31 and 0D32 identify this with the stated scheme-base condition.

proof.text: For the forward implication, $X$ is a scheme. The scheme relative-ample base-change theorem applies to each $T_i\to T$, so $X_i$ is a scheme and the ordinary pulled-back invertible module is ample over $T_i$. The Zariski/etale quasi-coherent equivalence identifies that ordinary pullback with the tensor pullback $L_i$ in the statement. This proves the forward implication.

Conversely assume every $L_i$ is relatively ample. Each $X_i$ is a scheme by hypothesis. Since absolute ampleness includes quasi-compactness, every inverse image of an affine open of $T_i$ is quasi-compact; hence $f_i$ is quasi-compact. The scheme canonical-Proj criterion implies that $f_i$ is separated. These scheme properties give the scheme-test meanings stated in the descent node. For an affine scheme $Z$ with a map $Z\to T_i$, the space $X_i\times_{T_i}Z$ is represented by the scheme fibre product, whose projection to $Z$ is quasi-compact by base change; so this scheme, the inverse image of the affine $Z$, is quasi-compact and is its own surjective etale atlas. For every scheme $W$ with a map $W\to X_i\times_{T_i}X_i$, the scheme test of the diagonal is the base change along it of the closed immersion $\Delta_{f_i}$, hence a closed immersion. Apply fpqc descent of these two properties to $f:X\to T$: it is quasi-compact and separated. Neither $X$ nor $T$ has been assumed quasi-compact as an absolute space.

Form $\mathcal A_d=f_*L^{\otimes d}$ and $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal A_d$. The graded quasi-coherent section-algebra theorem makes this a quasi-coherent graded Zariski algebra on $T$, interpreted on its small etale site by the scheme-site equivalence. The evaluation theorem supplies the graded homomorphism $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_dL^{\otimes d}$; each degree is the counit of pullback/direct image, and on local tensors evaluation is $a\otimes s\mapsto a\,s$. The line-module Proj-map theorem now supplies its open generation locus $U=U(\psi)$ and the canonical map $r:U\to P=\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$, where $P$ is a scheme.

Every $g_i:T_i\to T$ is flat. Apply flat direct-image base change to the quasi-coherent modules $L^{\otimes d}$, obtaining $g_i^*\mathcal A_d\simeq(f_i)_*L_i^{\otimes d}$. The canonical comparisons respect products and units: on local tensors the image of $(a\otimes s)(b\otimes t)$ is $ab\,(st)$, the product of $a\,s$ and $b\,t$, and $1\otimes1$ maps to $1$. They therefore assemble to a graded isomorphism $g_i^*\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal A_i$. By the counit definition of this comparison, its adjoint is precisely the pulled-back evaluation; thus $\psi$ pulls back to the evaluation $\psi_i$. The scheme-site equivalence and evaluation comparison identify these with the ordinary Zariski section algebra and evaluation on the scheme $X_i$.

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), flat base change and identification of the natural maps psi_d.

proof.text: The scheme canonical-Proj criterion applied to $(f_i,L_i)$ gives $U(\psi_i)=X_i$ and an open immersion $r_i:X_i\to\operatorname{Proj}_{T_i}(\mathcal A_i)$. The Proj-map theorem identifies $U(\psi_i)$ with the inverse image of $U$, and $r_i$ with the base change of $r$ under $P\times_TT_i\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_{T_i}(\mathcal A_i)$. To see $U=X$, represent any point of $X$ by $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$. The scheme fpqc base-change axiom makes $\{\operatorname{Spec}K\times_TT_i\to\operatorname{Spec}K\}$ an fpqc cover. Its joint surjectivity gives a point in some member; with its residue field $K'$ this is a map $\operatorname{Spec}K'\to\operatorname{Spec}K\times_TT_i$, hence by the fibre-product property a field-valued point $\operatorname{Spec}K'\to X_i$ whose composite to $X$ is $\operatorname{Spec}K'\to\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, so it represents the chosen point of $|X|$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Since the inverse image of $U$ is all of $X_i$, that point of $X$ lies in $U$. All points lie in the open subspace $U$, so $U=X$: for every scheme $V\to X$ the open immersion $U\times_XV\to V$ is surjective, since each point of $V$ gives a field-valued point of $X$ that factors through $U$ after a field extension, and a surjective open immersion is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), surjectivity loci and comparison of r with the local open immersions.

proof.text: The same scheme fpqc base-change axiom applied to $P\to T$ makes $\{P\times_TT_i\to P\}$ an fpqc cover. The base change of $r:X\to P$ to its ith member is $r_i$, an open immersion with scheme source. Fpqc descent of open immersions from spaces now identifies $X$ with an open subscheme of $P$. Thus $X$ is a scheme. The evaluation comparison identifies $\mathcal A$ and $\psi$ with the ordinary section algebra and ordinary evaluation for this scheme and its invertible module. Since $f$ is quasi-compact separated in the scheme-test sense and $X$ is now a scheme, $f$ is a quasi-compact scheme morphism (each $f^{-1}(V)$, $V\subseteq T$ affine, is the image of a quasi-compact etale atlas) and its diagonal is a closed immersion (test it on the scheme $X\times_TX$ itself), hence affine and quasi-compact, so $f$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. As $U(\psi)=X$ and its canonical map is an open immersion, the scheme canonical-Proj criterion implies that $L$ is ample over $T$. This proves the converse, including the asserted schematicity.
